`git merge` combines two histories without rewriting existing commits. If branches diverged, it usually creates a merge commit and preserves the original branch structure.

`git rebase` moves your branch’s commits onto a new base by replaying them. This creates new commit hashes and produces a cleaner, linear history.

Example on a feature branch:

```bash
git merge main    # incorporates main via a merge
git rebase main   # replays feature commits on top of main
```

Use merge when preserving history matters. Use rebase for a tidy local history, but avoid rebasing commits others already use because it rewrites history and may require a force-push.
